solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Being twenty, wayward wife is exchanged for one!

indicators.note: an exchange swaps one thing out and puts another in its place
something wayward strays from its proper course, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A twenty-year-old swaps an unfaithful wife for someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W of TWENTY for I, giving TENTYI, then rearrange. The comma makes 'twenty, wayward wife' look like a description of the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is a thing with distinct existence, a noun sense shared with the abstract noun for existence or a living thing.

clue.text: Even pole dancing is a cover-up

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, ending in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry remark that even pole dancing involves some concealment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' suggests a scandal being hushed up, but here it is meant literally: something that covers things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is a paper wrapper that encloses and hides a letter, so it literally covers things up.

clue.text: Boost to tourist city (not English)

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to leave out whatever follows, and English abbreviates to a single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Tourism gives a city a boost, with an aside about the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tourist city' is a cue for a famous resort, here the French Riviera one, and 'not English' strips the E abbreviation from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that invigorates or lifts the spirits, a direct synonym for a pick-me-up or boost.

clue.text: Politicians of old right put into trusses

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside that other thing

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
R is the abbreviation for right
to truss is to tie up, so trusses are ties

explanation.surface: Old-school right-wing politicians being trussed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Politicians of old' looks like the whole definition, but 'of' is the link and 'old' gives O, which with R goes inside TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, so they are a group of right-leaning politicians.

clue.text: Mark, clutching underwear, almost breaks open a barrel

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off
to clutch is to hold tightly, so one piece grips another inside it

blocks.note: a stain is a mark
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark, holding his underwear, nearly splits open a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a smudge or blot. In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Staves are the curved wooden planks of a barrel, and to stave in is to smash a hole by breaking them.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) Not Trump's favourite daily Sousa march

blocks.note: first meaning: a newspaper Trump often attacks
second meaning: a famous march by John Philip Sousa

explanation.surface: A newspaper Trump dislikes, linked to a rousing march.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans 5 down and 14 across. John Philip Sousa was the American bandmaster who wrote marches including one named after this paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington Post is a major American daily newspaper often critical of Trump, and Sousa wrote a march of that title in 1889.

clue.text: Peer cuts "vino" out?

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are put in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman cuts out the wine, or perhaps someone peers at a wine list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' could be a verb meaning look closely, but it is the noun for a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a rank of British nobility between earl and baron, so every viscount is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Pick-up expert, Norm, plagued with angst?

indicators.note: something plagued is troubled and disturbed, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A womaniser named Norm is tormented by anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-up expert' suggests a seducer good at chatting people up; it is someone who picks up heavy things.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongman is a performer or athlete who lifts very heavy weights, so lifting things up is his specialist skill.

clue.text: Hardly a celeb getting nothing but head?

blocks.note: first meaning: an unimportant, unknown person
second meaning, read cryptically: a head with no torso attached

explanation.surface: A minor figure gets nothing but oral sex, Private Eye style.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO BODY to see the second meaning: if all you have is a head, there is no body beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no fame or importance, the opposite of a celebrity.

clue.text: Lower chamber opening – odd relic

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are set in an unusual order

blocks.note: a vent is an opening
taken as written

explanation.surface: The opening of a lower house of parliament turns up a strange old relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower chamber' suggests a house of parliament such as the Commons; it is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The ventricles are the two lower pumping cavities of the heart, below the atria.

clue.text: Inconsistent DIY contractor's crap

indicators.note: something crap is badly made, so the letters are botched into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a do-it-yourself builder is erratic and rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor's' reads as possessive, but it is 'contractor is', and 'crap' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements that are contradictory clash with one another, which is what being inconsistent means.

clue.text: Possibly elder Republican interrupted Bush rashly

indicators.note: acting rashly is acting without order or care, so the letters are scrambled
an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so a piece is inserted

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An older Republican cuts in on President Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' and 'Bush' paint American politics, but the elder is a plant and Bush is just letters; a bush is also a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree or bush bearing elderflowers and berries, an example of a woody plant; 'Possibly' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Centre moved right of Labour leader in support of speaker

indicators.note: letters that are moved shift position and land in a new order
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken
being to the right of something means following it in a line of writing

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The political centre shifts rightward under a Labour leader, backing the Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre', 'right', 'Labour leader' and 'speaker' all sound like Westminster politics; the speaker is simply anyone giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a sloping stand on which a person giving a talk rests notes, so it supports whoever addresses an audience.

clue.text: Being tarted up, loved to cover Johnson's back

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
covering something wraps around it, so one piece goes outside another

blocks.note: to adore is to love deeply
last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Someone dolled up and adored covers for Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson's back' suggests supporting the politician; it just means the final letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To tart something up is to decorate it, often gaudily, and adorned likewise means decorated or embellished.

clue.text: see 5dn.
Chris M. was buggered – a sailor's handiwork

indicators.note: something buggered, in British slang, is broken or ruined, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude Private Eye jibe about a man called Chris M. and a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'was' looks like part of the sentence, but its letters belong in the fodder; 'buggered' is British slang for broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is carving done by whalers and seamen on bone or ivory to pass the time at sea.

clue.text: Most of the media, as far as Trump's concerned? Hence army mobilised

definitions.text: Most of the media, as far as Trump's concerned?

indicators.note: a mobilised force is moved into new positions, so the letters are redeployed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trump sees the press as hostile, so he calls out the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive question, and 'Hence army' reads as a consequence rather than the letters to reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump has repeatedly called the press 'the enemy of the people', casting it as his chief foe.

clue.text: Artificial bloke/ass, conserving energy

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep and preserve, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
both are mild terms for a foolish or socially inept person
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A robotic man or donkey that saves power.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN comes first, then NERD holding E. The slash just joins the two words for bloke and ass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannered style is affected and studied rather than natural, so it comes across as artificial.

clue.text: Outdoors, a large French supermarket fails to open

indicators.note: failing to open means the start is missing, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
FR is the abbreviation for French
Tesco is Britain's biggest supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A big French hypermarket stays shut, leaving shoppers outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French supermarket' looks like one item, but French gives FR and the supermarket is the British chain TESCO, which loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, borrowed from Italian, means in the open air, as in eating outside.

clue.text: Enormous cur, Niels Bohr, say?

blocks.note: first meaning: a giant breed of dog
second meaning: an eminent person from Denmark

explanation.walkthrough: Niels Bohr was the Danish physicist who modelled the atom, so he is a great man from Denmark; 'say' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed name is a very large dog, and read literally the phrase describes any distinguished Danish person.

clue.text: Arse-like, trivial book ditched

indicators.note: something ditched is thrown away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: banal means trite or trivial
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A crude review: a trivial, bum-like book that should be binned.
explanation.walkthrough: BANAL without its B. 'Arse' is British slang for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anal is the adjective relating to the anus, so it describes things of the backside.

clue.text: Beware sailors' den

blocks.note: cave is Latin for beware, a schoolboy warning cry
the Royal Navy's sailors

explanation.surface: A warning about a sailors' haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'cay-vee') was shouted in British schools as a lookout's warning. RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a wild animal's lair, often in a hollow underground, which is what a cavern is.

clue.text: Rolf reformed, once imprisoned, becoming a joint mover

indicators.note: to reform something is to shape it anew, so the letters take another form
a prisoner is held inside a cell, so one piece is shut within another

blocks.note: taken as written
an ex is a former one, so 'once' gives EX

explanation.surface: Rolf Harris, jailed and now reformed, takes a job moving joints.
explanation.walkthrough: The entertainer Rolf Harris was jailed in 2014. A 'joint mover' sounds like a drug dealer or furniture remover.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexor is a muscle that bends a limb at a joint, so its job is to move a joint.

clue.text: Rushdie hasn't begun a Conservative register

indicators.note: not having begun means lacking a start, so the first letter is missing

blocks.note: the novelist's first name
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Salman Rushdie hasn't yet signed up to the Conservative membership list.
explanation.walkthrough: You need the novelist's forename, SALMAN, not his surname, and then cut the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual book of records and tables, a kind of yearly register of facts.

clue.text: Satellite broadcast alerts after Trump's inauguration

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so only the first letter is used
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
coming after something means being written to the right of it

blocks.note: first letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Satellite TV carries news alerts following Trump's swearing-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inauguration' suggests the presidential ceremony; it means only the start of Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the 1962 communications satellite that relayed the first live transatlantic television pictures.

clue.text: God takes name "Spike"

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A deity adopts the nickname Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Spike' look like the name being taken, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp pointed growth on a plant stem, a natural spike or prickle.

clue.text: Anaesthetic hitch — temperature's dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left out, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: to hitch an animal is to tether it
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A problem during anaesthesia: the patient's temperature has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' looks like a snag in the procedure, but it is the verb for tying up, TETHER, which loses a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was one of the first general anaesthetics, inhaled to make surgical patients unconscious.

clue.text: Odious nob gets round ten debts

indicators.note: here it implies getting moved along a loop, so the leading letter travels to the back

blocks.note: a nob is an upper-class person, British slang
O is round in shape
X is the Roman numeral for ten
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A hateful posh man runs up ten unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' does double duty here, as the hint to cycle and as the letter O, a loose touch. A nob is British slang for a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious and odious both describe something extremely unpleasant or offensive, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Won round a former TV presenter with sex present

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Sir Robin Day was a famous British political interviewer on BBC television
S as in the sex box on a form, abbreviated loosely

explanation.surface: Someone wins over a retired TV host by offering sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a famous British TV interviewer of past decades. 'Present' looks like a gift or a verb; it is the adverb sense, at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present age, as opposed to the past, so it stands for 'at present'.

clue.text: Eleanor, firm, rough ride?

blocks.note: Eleanor Bron is an English actress and comedian
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An actress and her company give someone a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: You need the surname of Eleanor Bron, the English actress from Beyond the Fringe era satire and the Beatles film Help!
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed horse that bucks, so riding one gives a rough ride; the question mark flags the definition by example.
